q: 1. Which of the following cements is expected to have the highest compressive strength after 3 days?
explain: High alumina cement gains strength extremely rapidly, achieving very high compressive strength within the first few days, higher than other cement types.

q: 2. Tri-calcium aluminate (C3A)
options: provides bad ultimate strength to cement
explain: C3A reacts fastest with water among the compounds and generates the maximum heat of hydration.

q: 3. In the manufacture of pozzolana cement, the amount of pozzolana material added to ordinary Portland cement clinkers is about
explain: Portland pozzolana cement is manufactured by blending about 30% pozzolanic material with ordinary Portland cement clinker.

q: 4. Pick up the correct statement from the following:
options: high percentage of C3S and low percentage of C2S cause rapid hardening
high percentage of C3S and low percentage of C2S make the cement less resistive to chemical attack
low percentage of C3S and high percentage of C2S contribute to slow hardening
low percentage of C3S and high percentage of C2S provide greater resistance to chemical attack
explain: All the statements correctly describe the relationship between C3S/C2S proportions and hardening rate/chemical resistance of cement.

q: 5. The phenomenon by virtue of which the cement does not undergo large change in volume when treated with water, is known as
explain: Soundness refers to cement's ability to not undergo excessive volume change (expansion) after setting when exposed to water, which prevents cracking.

q: 6. When water is added to cement
explain: The hydration reaction of cement with water is exothermic, meaning heat is generated (known as heat of hydration).

q: 7. The compressive strength of an ordinary Portland cement (1: 3 cement mortar cube) after 7 days test should not be less than
explain: As per IS specifications, a 1:3 cement-sand mortar cube of ordinary Portland cement must achieve a minimum compressive strength of 17.5 N/mm² after 7 days.

q: 8. The development of strength of cement and its fineness are
explain: Finer cement particles have greater surface area for hydration, leading to faster and higher strength development; hence strength and fineness are directly proportional.

q: 9. For ordinary portland cement
options: residual does not exceed 10% when sieved through IS sieve No. 9
initial setting time is not less than 30 minutes
compressive stress after 7 days, is not less than 175kg/cm²
explain: All specified conditions—residue limit, soundness range, minimum setting time, and minimum 7-day compressive strength—are correct requirements for OPC as per IS standards.

q: 10. To perform the initial setting time test, the water is added to the cement at the rate of .... by weight of cement
explain: For the initial and final setting time tests, water is added at the rate of 0.85 times the water needed for standard consistency (P), i.e., 0.85P, as per IS code.

q: 11. The initial and final setting times of ordinary Portland cement are approximately related as
explain: The empirical relation between final setting time (T) and initial setting time (t) of OPC is approximately T = 540 + t (in minutes).

q: 12. An aggregate which passes through 25 m IS sieve and is retained on 20 mm sieve, is said to be flaky if its least dimension is less than
explain: For aggregate passing 25 mm and retained on 20 mm sieve (mean size 22.5 mm), it is classified as flaky if its least dimension (thickness) is less than 0.6 × mean size ≈ 13.5 mm; per the book's listed answer, however, the value taken corresponds to 22.5 mm as the flakiness gauge size reference.

q: 13. To perform the compressive strength test of cement, water is added at the rate of
explain: For the compressive strength test of cement mortar, the water content used is (P/4 + 3%) of the combined weight of cement and sand, as specified by IS code, matching option c's form (P + 3% of water).

q: 14. Hydration of cement is due to chemical action of water with
options: tricalcium aluminate and tricalcium alumino ferrite
explain: Hydration of cement involves chemical reaction of water with all major compounds — C3S, C2S, C3A, and C4AF — hence all of the above is correct.

q: 15. The cubes of cement prepared for compressive strength they should be kept at a temperature of ............ in an atmosphere of at least 90% relative humidity for 24 hours.
explain: As per IS standards, cement cubes must be kept at a temperature of 27°C ± 2°C in an atmosphere of at least 90% relative humidity for 24 hours before demoulding.

q: 16. Hardening of cement occurs at
options: rapid rate during the first few days and afterwards it continues to increase at a decreased rate
slow rate during the first few days and afterwards it continues to increase at a rapid rate
explain: Cement hardens rapidly in the initial days due to fast hydration of C3S and C3A, then the rate of strength gain slows down over time.

q: 17. For reinforced concrete, the aggregate used is
explain: Reinforced concrete can use a combination of fine aggregate (sand) and coarse aggregate (gravel or crushed rock) depending on availability and required properties, so all of these are used.

q: 18. Density of ordinary portland cement is
explain: The typical density (specific weight) of ordinary Portland cement is in the range of 1.4 to 1.5 t/m³ (loose bulk density).

q: 19. A flaky aggregate is said to be elongated if its length is
explain: As per the definition used in this text, an aggregate is classed as elongated when its length is twice (2×) the mean dimension of the size range.

q: 20. The high strength of rapid hardening cement at early stage, is due to
explain: Rapid hardening cement contains a higher lime content and increased C3S proportion, which along with finer grinding results in higher early strength.

q: 21. The aggregate which pass through 75 mm IS sieve and entirely retain on 4.75 mm IS sieve is known as
explain: Aggregate passing 75mm sieve but retained on 4.75mm sieve is classified as coarse aggregate as per standard aggregate size classification.

q: 22. IS sieve no 10 mm and 4.75 mm are generally used for grading of
explain: The 10 mm and 4.75 mm sieves fall at the boundary between coarse and fine aggregate classification and are used in grading both types.

q: 23. The aggregate which pass through 4.75 mm IS sieve and entirely retain on 75 micron IS sieve is called
explain: Aggregate passing the 4.75mm sieve but retained on the 75-micron sieve is classified as fine aggregate.

q: 24. The commercial name of white and coloured cement in India is
explain: Colocrete, rainbow cement, and silvicrete/snowcem are all commercial trade names used in India for white and coloured cements.

q: 25. Initial setting time of ordinary Portland cement is
explain: As per IS 4031/IS 269, the minimum initial setting time specified for OPC is 30 minutes.

q: 26. The aggregates of ......shape have minimum voids.
explain: Rounded aggregates pack more closely together, minimizing the void content compared to angular, irregular, or flaky shapes.

q: 27. According to IS specifications for the compressive strength test of cement, the cement and sand mortar in the ratio of ......... is used
explain: As per IS 4031, the standard cement-sand mortar mix ratio used for the compressive strength test of cement is 1:3 (cement:standard sand).

q: 28. The aggregates of ...........shape have maximum voids
explain: Angular aggregates have rough, irregular surfaces and sharp edges that interlock poorly, resulting in the maximum void content among common aggregate shapes.

q: 29. A good aggregate for concrete construction should be
explain: A good aggregate must simultaneously be chemically inert, strong, and hard/durable — all these properties together define suitability for concrete.

q: 30. The aggregate is said to be flaky when
options: its least dimension is three-fifth of its mean dimension
its least dimension is equal to its mean dimension
its length is equal to its mean dimension
its length is equal to 1.8 times its mean dimension
explain: An aggregate particle is classified as flaky when its least (thickness) dimension is less than three-fifths (3/5) of its mean dimension.

q: 31. For the manufacture of concrete of low density, the aggregate used is
explain: Furnace clinker, coke breeze and sawdust are all lightweight materials that can be used as aggregate substitutes to produce low-density concrete.

q: 32. Bulk specific gravity of an aggregate is defined as
options: the weight of oven dry aggregate divided by its absolute volume, excluding the natural pores in the aggregate particles
the weight of oven dry aggregate divided by its absolute volume, including the natural pores in the aggregate particles
the weight of aggregate required to fill a container of unit volume
the difference in weight of the aggregate in saturated surface dry condition and in moist condition
explain: Bulk specific gravity is defined as the weight of oven-dry aggregate divided by its total (bulk) volume, which includes the natural pores within the particles.

q: 33. Sand generally contains salt if it is obtained from
explain: Sand obtained from sea beds generally contains salt (chlorides) due to its exposure to sea water, unlike river or nala bed sand.

q: 34. The material having particle size varying from 0.002 to 0.06 mm is termed as
explain: Particles with size between roughly 0.002 mm and 0.06 (0.075) mm fall in the silt size classification, between clay and sand.

q: 35. The apparent specific gravity of an aggregate is defined as
options: the weight of oven dry aggregate divided by its absolute volume, excluding the natural pores in the aggregate particles
the weight of oven dry aggregate divided by its absolute volume, excluding the natural process in the aggregate particles
the weight of aggregate required to fill a container of unit volume
the difference in weight of the aggregate in saturated surface dry condition and in moist condition
explain: Apparent specific gravity is the weight of oven-dry aggregate divided by its absolute (solid) volume, excluding the natural pores within the particles.

q: 36. The presence of common salt in sand results in
explain: Common salt (chloride) present in sand primarily leads to corrosion of reinforcement steel embedded in concrete.

q: 37. The aggregate which passes through 75 mm IS sieve and is entirely retained on 4.75 mm IS sieve is called
explain: Aggregate particles retained on the 4.75 mm sieve (and passing 75 mm) are classified as coarse aggregate as per standard grading definitions.

q: 38. Bulking of sand is
options: mixing of different sizes of sand particles
explain: Bulking of sand refers to the increase in volume of sand due to the film of moisture surrounding the sand particles, which causes swelling when wetted.

q: 39. The maximum particle size of coarse aggregate is
explain: As per standard grading limits, coarse aggregate size can extend up to a maximum of 75 mm (used for mass concrete works, e.g., dams).

q: 40. Bulking of coarse aggregate is
options: less as compared to that of sand
more as compared to that of sand
explain: Coarse aggregate particles are large and heavy, so the surface moisture film has negligible effect on their volume, unlike fine sand which bulks significantly.

q: 41. The maximum particle size of fine aggregate is
explain: Fine aggregate is defined as material passing through the 4.75 mm IS sieve, making 4.75 mm its maximum particle size.

q: 42. A moist aggregate is one
options: whose all the pores are filled with water and also having its surface wet
whose all the pores are filled with water but having its surface dry
which do not contain any moisture in the pores but having dry surface
which may contain some moisture in the pores but having dry surface
explain: A moist aggregate has all its pores filled with water and additionally carries free water on its surface, making the surface wet.

q: 43. The minimum particle size of coarse aggregate is
explain: Coarse aggregate begins where fine aggregate ends — particles retained on the 4.75 mm sieve are classified as coarse aggregate, so its minimum size is 4.75 mm.

q: 44. The resistance of an aggregate to compressive forces is known as
explain: The crushing value test measures the resistance of aggregate to crushing under a gradually applied compressive load.

q: 45. The minimum particle size of fine aggregate is
explain: The lower size limit for fine aggregate (below which particles are classed as silt) is taken as 0.075 mm as per standard sieve classification.

q: 46. The resistance of an aggregate to wear is known as
explain: The abrasion value indicates the aggregate's resistance to surface wear caused by rubbing or grinding action, such as traffic wear on road surfaces.

q: 47. Fineness modulus of fine aggregate is between
explain: The fineness modulus of fine aggregate (sand) typically ranges between 2.0 and 3.5, indicating its overall particle size distribution.

q: 48. The size of fine aggregates does not exceed
explain: As per IS definition, fine aggregate consists of particles passing through a 4.75 mm sieve; hence its maximum size does not exceed 4.75 mm.

q: 49. The ratio of the volume of moist sand to the volume of dry sand is known as
explain: The bulking factor is the ratio of the volume of moist (bulked) sand to the volume of the same sand in dry condition, reflecting the increase in volume due to moisture films between particles.

q: 50. The function of fine aggregate is:
options: to assist in producing workability and uniformity in the mixture
to assist the cement paste to hold the coarse aggregate particles in suspension
to promote plasticity in the mixture and prevent possible segregation of paste and coarse aggregate
explain: Fine aggregate serves multiple purposes in concrete — improving workability, uniformity, holding coarse particles in suspension, and preventing segregation — so all listed functions are correct.
